name: HC-05
full_name: HC-05 Bluetooth Classic SPP Serial Module
description: Bluetooth Classic (v2.0+EDR) module providing a transparent serial (SPP) link over UART, configurable as master or slave - unlike the slave-only HC-06. It is controlled and configured through AT commands (entered by holding the EN/KEY pin high at power-up to enter command mode). The module core runs at 3.3 V; most breakout boards add a regulator so VCC accepts 3.6-6 V, but the UART logic is 3.3 V and the RXD pin should be level-shifted from a 5 V MCU.

pins.name: EN/KEY
pins.description: enable / command-mode select; hold HIGH at power-up to enter AT command mode

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: module supply, typically 3.6-6 V on breakout (onboard regulator); chip core is 3.3 V

pins.name: TXD
pins.description: UART transmit, 3.3 V logic (to MCU RX)

pins.name: RXD
pins.description: UART receive, 3.3 V logic (from MCU TX; level shift a 5 V MCU)

pins.name: STATE
pins.description: connection status output (high when a Bluetooth link is established)

typical_application: Wireless serial replacement between a microcontroller and a phone/PC: telemetry, remote control, and configuration over a Bluetooth SPP link.
gotchas: HC-05 can be master OR slave (set by AT command); the similar-looking HC-06 is slave-only - do not assume behavior from appearance
to enter AT command mode you must hold EN/KEY high (or press the onboard button) during power-up; in data mode AT commands are ignored
UART logic is 3.3 V: feed RXD from a 5 V MCU through a divider/level shifter, though TXD into a 5 V MCU usually reads fine
AT-mode baud differs from data-mode baud on many clones (often 38400 for AT, 9600 for data) - mismatched baud is the usual 'no response' cause
VCC range is the regulated breakout spec (3.6-6 V); the bare chip is 3.3 V, so never bypass the board regulator with raw 5 V to the chip
the STATE pin reflects link status and is useful to gate data; it is not a data line
